findings.text: The array teardown interface releases all internal nodes and leaves the array empty and unmarked, safe to discard or reuse.
The store interfaces insert or replace the entry at a given index and report the prior entry, with a locked form for external callers and an unlocked form for already synchronized contexts.
The erase interfaces remove the entry at a given index and report the removed value, with locked and caller-locked forms.
Bounce transfer state records completed page count alongside originating range start, range length, and kernel buffer location for resuming copies.
Per-open mirror state links a device, a page cache indexed by page number, an address space change subscription, mutual exclusion, and a flags word.
Device state combines character device linkage and zone classification with a growable chunk table under one mutex and allocation accounting plus free lists under a separate spin lock.
A memory chunk couples a page map descriptor with its owning device and a removal marker, while an interval subscription pairs a notifier with its owning mirror.
The test harness is sized for four mirror devices.
Each device memory chunk spans two hundred fifty six mebibytes.
Chunk table growth adds sixteen slots at a time.
The device mirror range fault timeout constant has value one thousand.
The page table tagging scheme reserves small odd tag values one and three for atomic and write markings.
Chunk table capacity, population, and slot storage are guarded by a dedicated mutex, while allocation counters and free page structures are guarded by a separate spin lock.
The per-mirror mutex serializes cached page table changes and fault insertion against invalidation; the invalidation path uses blocking acquisition when allowed and nonblocking attempt otherwise.
Store, erase, and destroy synchronize through the array lock, and the low level allocation helper requires that lock on entry.
When node allocation may sleep, the retry helper temporarily releases then reacquires the same interrupt, bottom half, or process context lock flavor before retrying.
The hexdump self check validates the formatting routine by comparing its output and length against an independent local model over randomized lengths and layouts, tallying total and failed cases.

The truncation check derives an expected length from layout geometry and ascii selection, then expects the routine to report full length while filling only the provided prefix and preserving the remainder pattern.
Bounce progress is monotonic within one command: the completed page count advances only after a page is copied and determines where the next fault or copy resumes.
The mirror page cache stores raw page identities without holding references and relies on range invalidation to discard stale entries over the affected span.
Private zone devices select device private migration while other devices select coherent migration, determined solely by device zone classification.
Device private pages resolve to their associated backing storage for migration and copying, while other pages resolve to themselves.

User read and write commands cycle between cached copy under lock and fault fill on missing or unwritable entries, repeating until the range completes or a fault fails, then finalize the completed count.
Range population retries on busy status and on concurrent invalidation detected via sequence validation, bounded by a time budget in the locked path and by a caller timeout in the unlocked path.
Chunk provisioning reserves backing address space according to zone type, expands the device table when full, maps pages, and publishes the new chunk before announcing capacity.
Module load runs randomized formatting and truncation sweeps across ascii modes and row widths, reports aggregate success, and signals failure via an error status; unload performs no action.

Opening creates per-file mirror state, initializes synchronization and cache, and subscribes to whole address space changes; release unsubscribes, evicts device memory, tears down the cache, and frees the state.
The interval notifier callback filters self-originated migration events, otherwise serializes, records the new sequence, and purges cached entries for the notified span.
Reads fail when a cached page is absent and writes additionally fail when the cached entry lacks write permission, triggering a fault and retry rather than partial use.
Advanced reserved entries are rejected on store, allocation failure without blocking retains an out of memory error, and stored errors propagate as the operation result.
Eviction skips pages that are not marked migratable and treats unexpected non-device pages as a warning condition while continuing with remaining pages.
Zero length destination handling and full buffer sweeps including boundary sizes are exercised, with any mismatch counted as failure toward the final status.
